reason: The sources provide sufficient details to support a surprising 45-second story with 12 verifiable claims.
story: Imagine a canyon so massive it could stretch all the way from New York City to Los Angeles. Valles Marineris on Mars is the solar system's largest canyon system, running nearly four thousand kilometers long and plunging up to seven kilometers deep—making it nearly four times deeper than Earth's Grand Canyon. Unlike the Grand Canyon, which was carved by a river, Mars basically tore its own crust apart. Around three and a half billion years ago, the immense weight and volcanic activity of the Tharsis bulge stressed the Martian crust until it cracked open. Later, colossal gravitational landslides widened the scar, sending debris rushing over a hundred kilometers across the canyon floor. Spacecraft have even discovered hydrated minerals and young volcanic cones hidden inside, proving this colossal Martian wound holds a complex, dynamic history.
angle: Valles Marineris is so large it could stretch across the entire continental United States from New York to Los Angeles.

claims.claim: Valles Marineris is a system of canyons spanning more than 4,000 kilometers long.
The canyon system is up to 7 kilometers deep.
The length of Valles Marineris is comparable to the distance from New York City to Los Angeles.
Valles Marineris is the largest canyon in the solar system.
The canyon system formed when the Tharsis volcanic bulge cracked the Martian crust.
Gravitational collapse and landslides significantly widened and deepened the canyon walls.
Some landslide deposits extend over 100 kilometers in length across the canyon floor.
Hydrated sulfate minerals like jarosite and gypsum have been detected within the canyon.
Valles Marineris was discovered by the Mariner 9 Mars orbiter of 1971-72.
Volcanic cones on the floor of Coprates Chasma are estimated to be 200 to 400 million years old.
The canyon reaches depths of up to 10 to 11 kilometers in certain regions like Coprates Chasma and Melas Chasma.

disputed: Whether the layered deposits inside the canyon represent ancient lake sediments, volcanic ash, or successive landslide sheets should be attributed in the script as scientific hypotheses under investigation.
